title: Product Photo Lighting Without a Studio | AIVideosUGC
description: Lighting for glass, metal, and shine, made from one uploaded photo. Soften a hard snapshot, say where the light comes from, and keep bright spots clean.
h1: Product Photo Lighting for Glass, Metal and Gloss
lead: Start from a frame where the highlight already falls on glass and metal, so a gloss phone case does not blow out. An AI avatar can present that case. You do not start from a blank page.
secondary_keywords: skincare product photo with soft light

steps.d: Choose the layout where light falls from the collar to the glass base. Nudge the bottle into that highlight.
Upload a photo showing the collar and base, or paste the product link. The wording names finishes such as brushed metal to match the shine.
Get captions beside the lit atomizer and a clip to post. A still costs 24 credits before running, and the editor shortens a hot streak.

faq.q: What does a product lighting template include?
faq.a: A frame that already puts a highlight on glass or metal. Drop in the lipstick tube. Someone on screen beside it is an AI avatar. You do not book a lighting crew to test the shine.

faq.q: How do I get a video out of the lighting template?
faq.a: Add the headphone photo and a sentence about the finish. A clip comes back that you can post. If the streak flares, pull that moment shorter before you post it.

faq.q: Why use a template instead of filming under real lights?
faq.a: Softboxes tie you to one room and one afternoon. A second highlight here is another render on the plan you already pay, and you can rename the finish after you watch the clip.
A one-person shop with a stack of glossy tins, or anyone selling a glass pitcher who needs an ad. You can make it without a lighting degree.

faq.q: Can I use it with no editing experience?
faq.a: Yes. A clear photo of the whole teapot is enough to begin, even if you have never edited a video.

faq.q: Which products belong in this template?
faq.a: Beauty, home, drink, gadgets, and other goods where the surface has to read. Change the product and the line when the audience changes.

faq.q: Can files I already own sit in the lit ad?
faq.a: Yes. A logo and a clip from an older shoot can join the new photo. The photo should show the finish you sell, including the streak you are trying to control.

faq.q: Where can the lit clip run?
faq.a: Use 3:4 for a portrait placement, 1:1 for a square tile, and 16:9 for a wide screen. Tall 9:16 and 4:3 are in the picker too. Instagram can take the square. A TikTok placement wants the tall file.

faq.q: Is payment required for a template?
faq.a: Yes. Templates are on a paid subscription. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A clip spends 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. A still spends 24 credits. Failed jobs return their credits.

faq.q: Can the lit clip go into paid ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. Client work and a product-page embed can both use it. Nothing is watermarked on the download. Stay inside the license on your plan.

faq.q: Why a template instead of building the light myself?
faq.a: This frame already has a streak, so your effort stays on the steel lid and the cooker you ship. Guessing that streak on a blank file is how a lid blows out.

steps.prompt: Give this white mug warm window light from the side and a soft shadow, with one clear bright spot on the shiny surface. Keep the rim, handle, and color as they are.

definition.title: What Is a Product Lighting Template?
paras: The highlight is already on the shiny surface, so a glazed mug does not turn into a blank white band.
You bring one picture that shows the glaze and the handle together. An AI avatar can stand next to that light. The mug in the clip still looks like the one you sell.

more_sections.h2: What the Lighting Template Can Carry
more_sections.lead: The same lit product can take a voice, a script, an avatar, and another version.

items.d: A voice talks through the product, or you clone a voice and reuse it on the next lit clip.
Captions can name the finish while the light plays across it.
You get a short script you can edit before the render.
An AI avatar you pick can present the lit product, and you can post the clip as your shop's ad.
One light can run across many photos from a product link or from your catalog API.
You can trim in the built-in editor, add a track from the music library, and repeat the clip in another language.
